docs.title: typechecks
docs.text: Check Python values at runtime and raise named errors when arguments have the wrong type. This is a small legacy utility, rather than a static type checker.

docs.title: Check and validate arguments
docs.text:
from typechecks import is_integer, is_string, require_integer, require_string

print(is_string("sample"), is_integer(3))
require_string("sample", name="label", nonempty=True)
require_integer(3, name="count")
try:
    require_string(3, name="label")
except TypeError as error:
    print(type(error).__name__)

True True
TypeError

The is_* functions return booleans. The require_* functions return None on success and raise TypeError for a mismatched type. An empty string with nonempty=True raises ValueError. name labels the argument in the error.

docs.title: Validate a collection
docs.text:
from typechecks import require_iterable_of

labels = ["tumor", "normal"]
require_iterable_of(labels, str, name="labels")
print("valid")

valid

Use a reusable sequence such as a list: this implementation may traverse the input twice when a value is invalid. It is unsuitable for validating one-shot iterators without first materializing them.

docs.title: Type semantics
docs.text:
Checks use isinstance(), so subclasses pass. Python booleans are integer subclasses: is_integer(True) returns True, and require_integer(True) succeeds. Integer validation does not check positivity or reject zero; make those value checks in your application.

Use require_instance(value, types, name=...) for another class or a tuple of classes. The API reference gives the actual supported arguments.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: Use predicates when invalid input is an ordinary branch; use validators when the caller should receive an exception. String validation additionally accepts nonempty=True. Integer validation has no positive/nonzero options.

docs.title: require_string
docs.text:
require_string(obj, name=None, nonempty=False)

Raise an exception if the obj is not of type str or unicode.

If name is provided it is used in the exception message.

If nonempty=True, then an exception is raised if the object is the empty string.

docs.title: require_integer
docs.text:
require_integer(obj, name=None)

Raise an exception if the obj is not of type int or long.

If name is provided it is used in the exception message.

This checks the type only; zero and negative integers are accepted.

docs.title: require_instance
docs.text:
require_instance(obj, types=None, name=None, type_name=None, truncate_at=80)

Raise an exception if obj is not an instance of one of the specified types.

Similarly to isinstance, 'types' may be either a single type or a tuple of types.

If name or type_name is provided, it is used in the exception message. The object's string representation is also included in the message, truncated to 'truncate_at' number of characters.

docs.title: require_iterable_of
docs.text:
require_iterable_of(objs, types, name=None, type_name=None, truncate_at=80)

Raise an exception if objs is not an iterable with each element an instance of one of the specified types.

See require_instance for descriptions of the other parameters.

docs.title: Documentation style
docs.text:
Follow the PyEnsembl writing guide and the mhctools example.

Put installation and the first useful example on the home page. Give complete imports and concrete inputs, explain the result, and state prerequisites before the reader runs a command. Show output only when it has been checked. Label replaceable paths and templates.

Order guides by common tasks before advanced setup and implementation details. Keep desktop sidebar groups expanded initially and individually collapsible. Split a page when a substantial task or reference needs its own explanation. Preserve useful old links and anchors when moving content.

Use ordinary text for concepts and library names; reserve inline code for literal commands, API names, parameters, paths and values. Keep qualifications, experimental status and scientific limitations beside the claims they qualify.

Use system fonts, a readable line length and restrained headings. Let wide tables and code blocks scroll inside their containers. Avoid repetitive navigation lists in prose and excessive callouts.

Install requirements-docs.txt and run ./docs.sh before opening a PR. Review the home page and a reference page at desktop and narrow widths. Run the repository's required lint and test commands and execute complete examples. Documentation dependencies are separate from runtime dependencies.
